A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a spaceborne monostatic-bisstatic formation can be designed in order to obtain a high quality stereoscopic effect, which can be exploited to measure the local relief with a metric precision, over a wide range in latitude.

the accuracy of monostaticbistatic stereo-radagrammetry can compete with the accuracy of SAR interferometry, but with some important differences: the first is a much lower sensitivity to the atmospheric phase delay, the second is the ability to work in areas where SAR interferometry is not applicable, and the third is the capability to work in the absence of a reference DEM, thus allowing the possibility to produce a DEM from scratch.

, by using the monostatic-bisatic configuration, the stereoscopic effect can be exploited to the utmost, and that the accuracy of the terrain elevation measurement can be improved up to a factor of 10 with respect to the monostatic configuration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of monostaticbistatic SAR data can provide a significant improvement in the reconstruction of the local surface relief.

a monostaticbistatic mission can be designed to achieve a high accuracy in surface relief reconstruction, and that the accuracy is comparable to that achievable with interferometric techniques, which, however, are limited to the acquisition of a pair of images.
the monostatic-bisatatic stereo-radargrmetry is an effective and accurate technique, able to provide a high resolution 3D view of the Earth's surface.
